Thought: To find the total electron count of KBr, I need to determine the number of electrons in each atom and add them together.

Potassium (K) has an atomic number of 19, which means it has 19 protons and 19 electrons.
Bromine (Br) has an atomic number of 35, which means it has 35 protons and 35 electrons.

The total electron count in KBr is the sum of electrons in both atoms:
19 (from K) + 35 (from Br) = 54 electrons
